blocks.text: Containers on the legacy default `bridge` network cannot resolve each other by name; user-defined bridges (including every Compose project network) provide embedded DNS.

rows: All default containers see each other

blocks.text:
$ docker run -d --name db -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=x postgres:17
$ docker run --rm alpine ping -c1 db
ping: bad address 'db'
$ docker network create ragnet
$ docker run -d --name db2 --network ragnet -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=x postgres:17
$ docker run --rm --network ragnet alpine ping -c1 db2      # resolves

items: Container IPs change on every recreate: never hard-code them.
This is why a stack "works in Compose but not with docker run": Compose always creates a user-defined network.

blocks.text: Q: "Two containers can't reach each other by name. Why?" A: "They're on the default bridge, which has no embedded DNS. Create a user-defined network and attach both, or use Compose, which does that automatically."

items: Name resolution needs a user-defined network.
